h: Castle Howard, coaster thrills and a foodie town
p: Eden Camp sits in a part of North Yorkshire that's packed with great days out, so it's easy to make a short break of it. Just west of Malton, Castle Howard is one of the grandest stately homes in England, with lakes, temples and vast grounds, plus an adventure playground for the kids. It was famously used as a filming location for Brideshead Revisited and makes a lovely contrast to the wartime huts.
If your family wants a bit more excitement, Flamingo Land at Kirby Misperton, a few miles north, combines a theme park with a zoo, with rides for thrill-seekers and animals to see in the same day.

Malton itself has earned a reputation as a foodie town, with independent producers, a regular food market and annual food festivals that draw crowds from across the region. Talbot Yard, a cluster of artisan food producers in a converted coaching yard, is a great place to pick up bread, coffee, cakes and more. The town is also known for its horse racing heritage, with racing stables in the surrounding area.

At Eden Camp, give yourself plenty of time, as the huts are full of detail and most people find themselves reading every story. Some of the displays are emotional, so it's worth chatting with children beforehand about what they'll see. The site is largely weatherproof, making it a handy option for a rainy day, while the nearby countryside of the Howardian Hills is perfect for a drive or a walk when the sun comes out.
